purpose: Keep monster JSON tiny. Family profiles carry anatomy and anti-drift intelligence; the universal engine derives complete generation identity.
rules: Family profile owns species anatomy, silhouette, head, body, surface, must-keep, must-avoid, accuracy checks, and known failure modes.
Monster recipes should only state what differs from the family.
Known family failure modes must be injected into generation and review, not merely stored.
Page recipes own scene-specific props, habitat interaction, pose/support, and story moment.
Family profile owns explicit limb/extremity structure, size impression, natural posture, visual behavior style, and environment fit in addition to anatomy and anti-drift rules.
Scene identity describes visual storytelling behavior, not combat mechanics; page recipes still own the exact action and interaction.
Variant scene_overrides are allowed only when a monster variant truly differs from its family behavior or environment fit.

Reusable scenery must never be copied into monster recipes. If another creature could use the same wall, floor, light, trap, furnishing, terrain form, lair dressing, or depth cue, the environment engine owns it.
Schema-v3+ recipes may contain only contract-approved top-level fields; duplicated resolved family fields are a CI failure.
A variant override should describe only the delta from family DNA. Do not restate the family silhouette, anatomy, must-keep, must-avoid, or accuracy checks unchanged.

Depicted weapons inherit universal equipment-state rules: a weapon associated with a creature must resolve to exactly one state—held in a believable grasp, visibly secured to the creature, or explicitly placed in the environment. Creatures without grasping limbs are exempt from hand-contact rules.
scalability_rule: Hundreds of monster recipes remain small. Creature files own identity, variant traits, behavior tendencies, locomotion, and habitat compatibility; reusable scenery belongs exclusively to the environment engine.

monster_may_define: variant-specific environment preferences when truly unique
environment_ownership.rule: If a visual element could be reused by another creature in the same place, it belongs in the universal environment engine: family/profile/component/overlay system.

recipe_policy.rule: Schema-v3+ monster files are recipes, not resolved creature documents. Family-owned anatomy, scene behavior, accuracy checks, references, and anti-drift knowledge must not be copied into them.
recipe_policy.migration_rule: Any legacy monster that already references a valid family_profile should be migrated to a schema-v3+ recipe unless it has a genuine variant difference that must remain as an override.
recipe_policy.size_rule: size and creature_type are permitted only when the variant genuinely differs from family taxonomy defaults.

equipment_physicality.rule: Creature gear identifies what belongs to the monster; the universal equipment engine resolves held versus secured versus environmental weapon state, prevents accidental duplicate weapons, enforces believable contact, and exempts creatures such as animated weapons that have no grasping limbs.
